title: Private: document + wire optional multi-region failover controls (supported deployments only)
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Private installer: adds documented (and values-wired) optional multi-region failover controls for supported Private deployments. Default remains disabled/monitor-only; enabling auto requires explicit operator action and external traffic steering.
body: Title: Private: document + wire optional multi-region failover controls (supported deployments only) Context: As part of the regional failover automation upgrade, we need a clear, supportable story for Private deployments. Some Private customers run multi-region (two+ clusters) and want the same control-plane semantics (monitor-only vs auto) with explicit operational caveats. This PR does NOT attempt to provide an end-to-end managed failover for Private; it documents what is supported, wires the config surface into the installer/values, and adds guardrails so we don’t accidentally imply that we control customer DNS/LB. Summary of changes: 1) Documentation: adds a new doc page and updates the main install guide describing (a) supported topologies, (b) prerequisites, (c) what the failover orchestrator can/can’t do in Private, and (d) recommended rollout path (disabled -> monitor -> auto). 2) Config wiring: adds Helm values + installer flags for failover mode and region metadata so the Private control plane can run the orchestrator in monitor-only mode by default and optionally enable auto transitions when explicitly configured. 3) Guardrails: validation rejects invalid configs (e.g., auto mode with <2 regions, missing primaryRegion, no capacity signal endpoint configured). Also adds an explicit “operatorAcknowledgement” string gate for auto mode so accidental enablement is harder. 4) Operational caveats: documents that DNS/edge traffic shifting is customer-managed in Private; we only update internal routing policy/state and emit audit/events. If the deployment doesn’t have a traffic manager capable of steering across regions, failover will be limited to the region behind the customer’s entrypoint. Details: New/updated config keys (Helm values / installer config): - failover.enabled: boolean (default false) - failover.mode: "disabled" | "monitor" | "auto" (default "disabled"; installer allows setting "monitor" but requires acknowledgement for "auto") - failover.primaryRegion: string (required when enabled) - failover.regions: comma-separated list of region IDs (required when enabled; must be length >= 2 for auto) - failover.progressive.canaryPercent: integer (default 5; used only in auto) - failover.safeToFailover.requireCapacityCheck: boolean (default true) - failover.safeToFailover.capacitySignalEndpoint: URL (required when capacity check is enabled) - failover.audit.sink: "stdout" | "http" | "s3" (default "stdout"; http requires failover.audit.httpEndpoint) - failover.operatorAcknowledgement: string (required when mode=auto; doc explains it should include change ticket ID + approver) Installer behavior notes: - We do not configure external DNS/LB (F5, Route53, Cloudflare, etc.) in Private. Docs call out that customers must integrate their own traffic steering with our failover events (webhook/audit sink) if they want entrypoint failover. - In air-gapped installs, “capacitySignalEndpoint” can be internal-only; docs include example service DNS and required network policies. - The orchestrator will run in monitor mode if enabled without auto; it evaluates signals and emits recommended actions but will not change routing policy. Upgrade / rollout guidance (added to docs): - Start with mode=monitor for at least one week; verify region health signals are present and that recommended actions are reasonable (no flapping). - Run at least one staging controlled failover before enabling auto in production. - For production, start with canaryPercent 1–5% and restrict to low-risk routes/models; increase only after observing stable SLO recovery. - Ensure target region has headroom (GPU pool, queue depth) and that dependencies are healthy; safe-to-failover checks will prevent transitions but operators should still validate during change window. - Keep manual override path available (documented) and define who has RBAC to use it (ties to INT-881). Files / areas changed (high level): - docs/private/multi-region-failover.md (new) - docs/private/installation.md (updated) - charts/redwood-private/values.yaml (new defaults + comments) - charts/redwood-private/templates/failover-orchestrator-configmap.yaml (wiring) - installer/config/schema.yaml (validation + mode gates) - installer/cmd/root.go (flags: --failover-mode, --regions, --primary-region, --operator-ack) - examples/private/values.failover-monitor.yaml (new) - examples/private/values.failover-auto.yaml (new, explicit warnings) Example snippet (docs): values.yaml: failover: enabled: true mode: monitor primaryRegion: us-east-1 regions: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"] safeToFailover: requireCapacityCheck: true capacitySignalEndpoint: "http://capacity-signal.svc.cluster.local:8080" audit: sink: stdout Notes: - Switching to mode=auto requires failover.operatorAcknowledgement and two+ regions. - For Private, external DNS/LB steering is out of scope; integrate via audit webhook if desired. Checklist: - [x] Defaults are safe (disabled unless explicitly enabled) - [x] Monitor-only documented as first step - [x] Auto enablement requires explicit acknowledgement string - [x] Validation catches common misconfigurations - [x] Docs include “what we don’t do” to avoid overselling - [x] Links to runbook + game day plan (internal references) Review conversation (highlights): - Tomáš Novák: Please add a clearer “stop conditions / rollback” section for Private operators and link to the automated failover runbook. -> Updated docs with rollback steps and a “disable automation” command/flag; added internal link reference used by Support. - Connor O’Brien: Can we prevent auto mode from being enabled via values alone without some explicit knob? We’ve been burned by copy/paste. -> Added failover.operatorAcknowledgement requirement and schema validation; examples include bold warnings and use a placeholder that will fail validation unless edited. - Miles Thornton: Make sure we’re precise that in Private we only update internal routing policy (and optionally emit events), not DNS. -> Added explicit caveat section and updated wording throughout (“traffic steering is customer-managed”). - Irene Choi: For air-gapped installs, call out network policy requirements for the capacity signal endpoint and audit webhook. -> Added a short “Networking requirements” subsection with recommended service DNS and ports, plus note on restricting egress. CI / checks: - build-installer (linux/amd64): pass - chart-lint: pass - docs-link-check: pass - e2e-install (kind): pass Merge: Squash merged to main. Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Add a small “failover event webhook” example integration for common traffic managers (Linear ENG-2853 candidate). - Consider adding a UI surface in the Private admin console to show failover mode/state (outside installer scope).
